guidance.statement: Group EBITDA margin normalises to slightly over 22% excluding one-time UK acquisition costs
Clinics and insurance cash burn to continue at a similar run rate next year
Cayman insurance losses to reduce significantly over the next 3 quarters
Committed ₹3,000 Cr of projects over the next two years, part own cash and part borrowing
No meaningful bed additions for the next two to three years
Southwest Bangalore 100-bed hospital to start by end of Q2
UK private payer mix to move from 95% NHS toward about 70% NHS over 4-5 years
Average length of stay to come down to between 3.9 and 4 from 4.3 in Q1

operating_notes.text: India hospital EBITDA margin was 25.1% in Q4FY26 versus 21.5% a year earlier, helped by robotic cardiac surgeries (~100/month) and higher-end procedures.
Cayman insurance loss ratio was 110-112% (claims paid divided by premiums net of reinsurance) with annualised premium run-rate of USD 60 million.
Clinics and insurance losses were around ₹66 Cr in FY26; 11 clinics in Bangalore, with plans to double the count and enter Kolkata in FY27.
India clinic network did about 66,000 consultations in Q1FY27, up about 30% YoY, and clinic footfalls are roughly 30% of hospital OPD footfalls.
Cayman insurance is running at about a USD 60 million annualised book, with July renewals seeing 100% acceptance at higher prices.
India clinic business lost about ₹15 Cr in Q1FY27, disclosed in the IR deck.

timeline.summary: On its 26 May 2026 Q4FY26 call, Narayana Health reported India hospital margin of 25.1% against 21.5% a year earlier, group margin of about 20% (over 22% excluding one-time UK acquisition costs), and ₹3,000 Cr of proposed capex.

On its 3 August 2026 Q1FY27 earnings call, Narayana Hrudayalaya said India net margin expanded 400 bps YoY, Cayman insurance losses narrowed to about USD 3.7 million, and it has committed ₹3,000 Cr to projects over the next two years.
